parameters.content:
## Workflow F — Outcome Follow-up Scheduler (Twilio)

Stage 2 of the two-stage feedback flow. Workflow B asks "Will you do this?";
Workflow C records the answer; **this** workflow sends the delayed
"Were you able to complete it?" and closes windows that expired unanswered.

### Why this is its own workflow
Workflow B's responsibility is *clinician-approved dated nudges due now*. The
outcome check is neither approved content nor dated — it is a feedback event
whose timing is derived from a delivery that already happened. Folding it into B
would mean B reading `schedule_state` as a second trigger source and would blur
the line the review portal depends on: everything B sends was approved by a
clinician. Nothing here creates a row in `nudges`.

### Every 5 minutes, in `Australia/Melbourne`
1. **Send due outcome checks.** `status=awaiting_followup` AND
   `commitment_response=YES` AND `followup_due_at <= now` AND
   `followup_sent_at` empty AND the patient is still `active`.
2. **Expire unanswered commitments.** `status=awaiting_commitment` with no
   `commitment_response` once `followup_due_at` passes → `no_feedback` /
   `commitment_response=NO_FEEDBACK`. Never `NOT_YET` — silence is not a
   self-report, and conflating them would corrupt the adherence measure.
3. **Expire unanswered outcomes.** `status=awaiting_followup` whose check was
   sent more than `FOLLOWUP_OUTCOME_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 24) ago with no
   `outcome_response` → `no_feedback` / `outcome_response=NO_FEEDBACK`.

### Exactly-once delivery
`followup_sent_at` and `followup_wa_id` are the claim check: a row that has
either is skipped. A duplicate or overlapping scheduler execution therefore
re-reads the row, finds it claimed, and sends nothing. The window is *not* a
five-minute band as in Workflow B — a due follow-up stays eligible until it is
actually sent, so a missed tick delays it rather than dropping it.

### Late Yes
`followup_due_at` is computed once by Workflow B from the delivery timestamp,
not from the moment the patient answers. A Yes arriving after the due time makes
the row immediately eligible on the next tick; a Yes arriving before it waits.

### STOP
Workflow C sets `status=opted_out` and clears `followup_due_at` on every open
row, so an opted-out patient fails all three eligibility guards here.

### Required environment variables
`GOOGLE_SHEETS_SPREADSHEET_ID`, `TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID`, `TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`,
`TWILIO_WHATSAPP_FROM`, `TWILIO_OUTCOME_CONTENT_SID`.
Optional: `FOLLOWUP_OUTCOME_WINDOW_HOURS` (default 24).

`TWILIO_OUTCOME_CONTENT_SID` is a placeholder until the Done / Not yet
quick-reply Content Template is created — see `docs/TWILIO_CONTENT_TEMPLATES.md`.

### Safety
Keep this workflow **inactive** until the Sheet migration is applied and both
Content Templates exist. Activating it against an unmigrated Sheet is harmless
(no row can satisfy the guards) but it will read the spreadsheet every 5 minutes.
